q: and went and dwelt at Thyrea in Argolis, which the Lacedæmonians gave them.

s: Ægina is difficult to access rocks and sunken reefs (around the island beneath the sea)
q: Of all the Greek islands Ægina is the most difficult of access. For there are rocks under the sea all round it, and sunken reefs.

s: Æacus has hall named Hall of Æacus (in the most conspicuous part of the city)
q: in the most conspicuous part of the city what is called the Hall of Æacus

s: Æacus receive suppliants envoys to Æacus (during a drought in Greece)
q: Accordingly they sent envoys from every city to beg Æacus to do so.

s: Epidaurus contains Dionysus (a temple)
q: And there are temples of Dionysus and Artemis, the latter as a Huntress.

s: Æacus propitiate Pan-Hellenian Zeus (to bring rain to Greece)
q: And he offered sacrifices and prayers to Pan-Hellenian Zeus and caused rain to come on the earth

s: Phocus has tomb Phocus's tomb (near the Hall of Æacus)
q: And near the Hall of Æacus is the tomb of Phocus, a mound of earth with a base in the shape of a circle

s: Phocus is son of Thetis (according to Greek tradition)
q: and Phocus was the son of her sister Thetis, if the Greeks speak the truth.

s: Peleus kill Phocus (by deliberately throwing a quoit at him)
q: he purposely threw it at Phocus and hit him.

s: Hecate is honoured by Æginetans (more than any other god)
q: And of all the gods the people of Ægina honour Hecate most

s: Hecate has statue by Myron (a wooden statue with one head and one body)
q: containing a wooden statue of Hecate by Myron, with only one head and one body.

s: Epidaurus contains Artemis (as a Huntress)
q: And there are temples of Dionysus and Artemis, the latter as a Huntress.

s: Alcamenes make Hecate Epipurgidia (the first to make Hecate with three heads and three bodies)
q: Alcamenes as it seems to me was the first who made the statue of Hecate with three heads and three bodies which the Athenians call Hecate Epipurgidia

s: Aphæa is worshipped at temple of Aphæa (on Ægina near Mount Pan-Hellenium)
q: And in Ægina as you go to the mountain of Pan-Hellenian Zeus is the temple of Aphæa

s: Artemis Issora is daughter of Zeus (by Carme)
q: that Britomartis was the daughter of Zeus by Carme the daughter of Eubulus

s: Artemis Issora is associated with Artemis (as a very great friend)
q: and was a very great friend of Artemis.

s: Artemis Issora is called Aphæa (in Ægina)
q: And she is called Aphæa in Ægina, but Dictynna in Crete.

s: Artemis Issora is called Dictynna (in Crete)
q: And she is called Aphæa in Ægina, but Dictynna in Crete.

s: Trœzen contains Artemis the Saviour (a temple and statues in the market-place)
q: In the market-place is a temple, and statues, of Artemis the Saviour.

s: Theseus build Artemis the Saviour (after returning from Crete)
q: And it is said that Theseus built it and called her Saviour, when he returned from Crete after having killed Asterion the son of Minos.

s: Pittheus has monument at Trœzen (behind the temple of Artemis the Saviour)
q: And behind the temple there is a monument of Pittheus, and three seats are on it of white stone

s: Pittheus teach Muses (the art of language at the temple of the Muses)
q: Here they say Pittheus taught the art of language

s: Epidaurus contains Aphrodite (a temple)
q: There is a temple also built to Aphrodite

s: Pittheus build Thearian Apollo (the oldest temple known to the narrator)
q: And they say Pittheus built the temple of Thearian Apollo, which is the oldest of all I know.

s: Orestes is received at here (before he was cleared of his mother’s blood)
q: For before he was cleared of his mother’s blood, none of the people of Trœzen would receive him in their houses: but they put him here and gradually cleared him and fed him here, till the expiatory rites were completed.

s: Orestes use water from Hippocrene (among his purgations)
q: And they say that Orestes among other purgations used water from Hippocrene.

s: Epidaurus contains Hera (a temple near the harbour on a sea cliff)
q: and near the harbour on the cliff jutting out into the sea is they say one of Hera.

s: Epidaurus contains Cissæan Athene (a wooden statue in the citadel)
q: And the Athene in the citadel, a wooden statue well worth seeing, they call Cissæan Athene.

s: Æginetans inhabit Ægina (the island opposite Epidauria)
q: The Æginetans inhabit the island opposite Epidauria.

s: Ægina has old name Œnone (before it was named after Ægina)
q: it was called Ægina after her instead of its old name Œnone

s: Zeus is asked for settlers
q: and when Æacus was grown up he asked of Zeus for settlers

s: Hippolytus is a son of Theseus
q: And Hippolytus the son of Theseus has precincts and a temple in them and ancient statue.

s: Diomede establishes Pythian games (in honour of Apollo)
q: they say also that Diomede first established the Pythian games in honour of Apollo.

s: Phædra gazes at Hippolytus (while he was training, because she loved him)
q: where, when Hippolytus was training, Phædra would gaze at him in her love.

s: Hippolytus’ myrtle has leaves pricked by Phædra (in anguish over her love for Hippolytus)
q: Here too grows the myrtle with the leaves pricked, as I described before: for when Phædra was in despair and found no relief for her love-pains, she wreaked her agony on the leaves of the myrtle.

s: Æsculapius is represented by Hippolytus (according to the people of Trœzen; the statue was made by Timotheus)
q: but the people of Trœzen say it is not Æsculapius but Hippolytus.

s: Well of Hercules is discovered by Hercules (according to the people of Trœzen)
q: in front of it is what is called the Well of Hercules, the water (as the people of Trœzen say) which Hercules discovered.

s: Hippolytus has precinct Temple of Hippolytus
q: And Hippolytus the son of Theseus has precincts and a temple in them and ancient statue.

s: Athenian plague presses on Athens (severely)
q: which brought about deliverance from the plague, which pressed so hard on the Athenians.

s: Halicarnassus builds temple for Trœzen (the temple of Isis)
q: the temple the Halicarnassians built for Trœzen their mother city

s: Theseus finds under Theseus’ rock (Ægeus’ shoes and sword)
q: because Theseus found under it the shoes and sword of Ægeus.

s: Theseus’ sword and shoes belong to Ægeus
q: because Theseus found under it the shoes and sword of Ægeus.

s: Bridal Aphrodite is built by Theseus (when Theseus married Helen)
q: near this rock is the temple of Bridal Aphrodite, which was built by Theseus when he married Helen.

s: Fruit-giving Poseidon has temple at Trœzen (outside the walls)
q: And outside the walls is a temple of Fruit-giving Poseidon

s: Poseidon threatens Trœzen (in anger, by casting brine on seeds and plant roots)
q: for they say that Poseidon in wrath threatened to make their land fruitless, by casting brine on the seeds and roots of their plants

s: Natal-place is where Theseus (according to the people of Trœzen)
q: the place which they call Natal-place, because they say Theseus was born there.

s: Temple of Hippolytus has priest Hippolytus (serves for life)
q: and the people of Trœzen have a priest of Hippolytus who serves for life

s: Troezenian maidens dedicate maiden girdle to Athene (before marriage, at Sacred Island)
q: she also imposed the custom on the maidens of Trœzen that they should before marriage dedicate their maiden-girdle to

s: Calaurea is sacred to Apollo (in ancient days)
q: And they say the island Calaurea was in ancient days sacred to Apollo

s: Poseidon has temple on Calaurea (with a maiden priestess until marriage)
q: There is also at Calaurea a sacred temple to Poseidon, and the priestess is a maiden till the period for marriage.

s: Demosthenes is exonerated from receiving Harpalus’ money (Philoxenus’ letters omitted him from the recipients)
q: Although in those letters he enumerated the names of those who had had any money from Harpalus, and the precise sum which each of them had, he made no mention whatever of Demosthenes

s: Methana has Methana warm baths (about 30 stades away)
q: And at the distance of about 30 stades from this small town are some warm baths.

s: Dorians colonize Hermione (from Argos, amicably according to the narrator)
q: And afterwards Dorians from Argos colonized Hermione, but amicably I think

s: Hippolytus is called in heaven Charioteer (according to the people of Trœzen)
q: but they try to make out that Hippolytus is called in heaven the Charioteer, and has this honour from the gods.

s: Marine Aphrodite has temple Hermione
q: what I select as most worthy of record are the temple of Marine Aphrodite and Aphrodite of the Harbour

s: Aphrodite receives sacrifice from maidens and widows (before marriage, at Hermione)
q: there is another temple of Aphrodite, which has other honours from the people of Hermione and this special one, that maidens or widows intending to marry must all sacrifice here before their marriage.

s: Hermione has temple of Dionysus Melanægis
q: And next is a temple of Dionysus Melanægis, in whose honour they have a musical contest every year, and give prizes for diving and rowing.

s: Temenium is a fortified place (occupied and fortified by Temenus)
q: he occupied and fortified the place, when he fought with the Dorians against Tisamenus and the Achæans from this base

s: Temenium belongs to Argives (in the narrator’s day)
q: Temenium--now Temenium belongs to the Argives

s: Temenus is son of Aristomachus
q: Temenus the son of Aristomachus

s: Temenus occupies and fortifies Temenium (as a base against Tisamenus and the Achæans)
q: for he occupied and fortified the place

s: Temenium has temple of Poseidon
q: there is a temple of Poseidon at Temenium and another of Aphrodite

s: Temenium has temple of Aphrodite
q: there is a temple of Poseidon at Temenium and another of Aphrodite

s: Nauplia has temple of Poseidon
q: And there are still some remains of walls at Nauplia, and a temple of Poseidon and a harbour

s: Canathus is bathing place of Hera (Hera bathes there yearly and becomes a virgin again, according to Argive tradition)
q: in which the Argives say Hera bathes every year and becomes a virgin again.

s: Hermione has temples of Apollo (three temples and three statues)
q: And there are three temples and three statues of Apollo: one has no title, the second is called Pythæan Apollo, and the third Apollo of the Borders.

s: Genesium has temple of Poseidon (small temple near the sea)
q: near the sea close to Genesium there is a small temple of Poseidon.

s: Landing-place is landing place of Danaus (first landing in Argolis, according to tradition)
q: according to tradition this was the first place in Argolis where Danaus and his sons landed.

s: Thyrea is a place of battle (site of the contest between 300 Argives and 300 Lacedæmonians)
q: there is a place called Thyrea, where 300 picked men of the Argives fought with 300 picked men of the Lacedæmonians for the possession of the land.

s: Thyrea is recovered by Argives (the Argives claim they recovered it justly by conquest)
q: And in my day the Argives inhabited the district of Thyrea, and they say that they recovered it justly by conquest.

s: Æginetans receive Thyrea (given the district by the Lacedæmonians after being expelled from Ægina)
q: and afterwards gave it to the Æginetans who had been driven out of Ægina by the Athenians.

s: Æginetans are expelled from Ægina (by the Athenians)
q: the Æginetans who had been driven out of Ægina by the Athenians.

s: Apollo has epithet Lycian Apollo
q: the second is called Pythæan Apollo

s: Polemocrates is son of Machaon
q: He was the son of Machaon, and brother of Alexanor

s: Polemocrates is brother of Alexanor
q: He was the son of Machaon, and brother of Alexanor

s: Parnon is boundary between Lacedæmonians (also borders Argives and people of Tegea)
q: beyond these villages extends Mount Parnon, which is the boundary between the Lacedæmonians and Argives and people of Tegea.

s: Apollo has epithet Apollo of the Borders
q: and the third Apollo of the Borders.

s: Lycian Apollo name is borrowed from Argives (according to Telesilla)
q: The name Pythæan they borrowed from the Argives

s: Pythæus is son of Apollo
q: for Telesilla says that to their country first of all the Greeks came Pythæus the son of Apollo.

s: Hermione has temple of Fortune (latest temple of the people)
q: And the temple of Fortune is they say the latest one that the people of Hermione have

s: Hermione has well old well of Hermione (fed by a hidden channel and never runs dry)
q: And they have two wells, one an old one into which the water flows by a hidden channel, but it would never grow dry, not even if all the population were to come and drink of it

s: Hermione has well Meadow well (dug in the narrator’s day)
q: and another dug in our day, and the name of the place from which the water flows into it is Meadow.

s: Hermione has temple of Demeter (on Pron; most worthy of notice)
q: But the temple most worthy of notice is that of Demeter on the Pron.

s: Pron contains temple of Demeter
q: But the temple most worthy of notice is that of Demeter on the Pron.

s: Atheras offers hospitality to Demeter (when Demeter came to Argolis)
q: Atheras and Mysius offered the goddess hospitality

s: Mysius offers hospitality to Demeter (when Demeter came to Argolis)
q: Atheras and Mysius offered the goddess hospitality

s: Colontas is father of Demeter Chthonia
q: Colontas would neither receive her into his house, nor pay her any other attention: and in this he acted very much against the wish of his daughter Chthonia.

s: Demeter Chthonia is conveyed to Hermione (by Demeter)
q: but Chthonia was conveyed to Hermione by Demeter, and built the temple there to Demeter.

s: Demeter Chthonia is epithet of Demeter (at Hermione)
q: And Demeter is called Chthonia there

s: Chthonia festival honours Demeter (annual summer festival)
q: the annual festival held in her honour in the season of summer is called Chthonia too.
